clue.text: Ruin course

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to spoil someone's chances, as in a hope being scuppered
second meaning: one course of a meal

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, two separate meanings of one short word: a verb for wrecking hopes and a noun for food served at a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dish someone's chances is colloquially to wreck them, and a dish is also one course served at dinner.

clue.text: Dispirited county players

explanation.surface: A county team's players are glum after a defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast is a standard synonym for dejected, describing someone low in spirits.

clue.text: Wetsuit in vessel

definitions.meaning: surfers' slang for a full-length wetsuit

explanation.surface: Someone sits aboard a boat wearing their wetsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surfing sense is less familiar: a thick full wetsuit is called this because the wearer heats up inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Surfers use the word for a full-body wetsuit, and it is also an ordinary name for a steam-powered ship.

clue.text: What playwright has to put on vessel

parts.note: to stage a play is to put it on

explanation.surface: A dramatist must mount a production aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' reads as obligation; the definition stops at 'has', and 'to' joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical skill, the technique of writing for and presenting on the stage, is what a good dramatist possesses.

clue.text: Stupid person hung up key for a small kitchen tool

indicators.note: in a down clue, hung up means turned upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a key is something that opens

explanation.surface: A fool hangs up a key next to a kitchen gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin-opener is a small handheld kitchen device for cutting into cans.

clue.text: Rex enters to receive a girl

indicators.note: something that enters goes inside, so the king's letter is placed within the other word

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, king

explanation.surface: A man called Rex comes in to welcome a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex looks like a man's name, but it is Latin for king, abbreviated R.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta is a female first name, and crosswords often define names simply as girl.

clue.text: Join one section in US state

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a cut is a section or slice

explanation.surface: Someone joins one section of a group in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Connecticut is one of the New England states of the USA.

clue.text: An hotel rebuilt in Irish town

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hotel has been rebuilt in a town in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Athlone is a town on the River Shannon in the Irish midlands.

clue.text: Kate off to secure work in state capital

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside, so one piece goes within the other
off means gone bad or awry, so these letters are not in their proper order

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Kate departs to land a job in a state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like Kate leaving, but it signals her name is jumbled; OP (opus) then sits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Topeka is the capital city of the US state of Kansas.

clue.text: She served king in original revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards
in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A woman served her monarch during the first revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: A Wren was a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service, the British women's navy, so she served the Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wren is a woman who served in the Royal Navy's women's branch, hence 'She served'.

clue.text: He's in print cunningly exposing a practical training programme

indicators.note: doing something cunningly means artfully twisting it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man cleverly exposes a training scheme in the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: An internship is a period of supervised work experience for trainees or students.

clue.text: Ordinary reserve — one may be full of memorable sayings

definitions.text: one may be full of memorable sayings

explanation.surface: An unremarkable reserve player is someone full of quotable lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A commonplace book is a notebook in which a person copies quotations and striking passages.

clue.text: Frank, composer, must attend court to discover finding

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Frank, a composer, has to go to court to learn the result.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name but means candid.
explanation.definitionFit: An open verdict is an inquest's formal conclusion when the cause of death cannot be determined, a legal finding.

clue.text: Onset of stress? Give encouragement to one used to working in the theatre

definitions.text: one used to working in the theatre

indicators.note: the onset of anything is its beginning, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: An actor under stress is cheered on before a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests the stage, but it is the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons operate in a hospital's operating theatre, so they work there routinely.

clue.text: One has to be brought in to satisfy composer

indicators.text: has to be brought in to
indicators.note: being brought in to something means being placed within it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone must be called in to please a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer, known for the Gymnopédies.

clue.text: A trifle in glass?

parts.note: surface reading: a dessert of sponge, custard and cream served in a glass bowl
setter's reading: something unimportant, and also a modest measure of ale in a glass

explanation.walkthrough: A trifle is a British layered pudding often served in a glass dish, but here it means something of little consequence.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something trivial, and literally a weak or small drink of ale served in a glass.

clue.text: Young woman, in hectic year, becomes a spy

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
hectic means frantic and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a miss is a young woman

explanation.surface: A girl turns to espionage during a frantic year.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is an agent sent on a mission, and the word can also mean a secret agent or spy.

clue.text: Bay on right will give shelter

parts.note: a cove is a small bay
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A bay on the right-hand side of the coast offers protection.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover someone is to protect or screen them, offering shelter.

clue.text: Unrehearsed ending to the comic operetta

parts.note: a candid photo is unposed, unrehearsed

indicators.note: an ending is the final part, so only the closing letter is taken

explanation.surface: A comic operetta gets an improvised finale.
explanation.definitionFit: Candide is Leonard Bernstein's comic operetta based on Voltaire's satirical novel.

clue.text: Declare after a century, getting applause

indicators.note: after places the word for declare behind the other pieces

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to claim is to declare or assert

explanation.surface: A batsman declares the innings after scoring a hundred and is cheered.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a century is a hundred runs and to declare is to end an innings voluntarily.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclaim is enthusiastic public praise, much like applause.

clue.text: Assistant in a small company, reportedly mild

parts.note: CO is the short form of company

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word for mild is taken by its sound

parts.note: mild, as in a mild or light beer

explanation.surface: An assistant at a small firm is said to be gentle.
explanation.walkthrough: Mild and light are both British beer styles, which is the link between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte is an assistant or follower, originally one helping a priest at the altar.

clue.text: A bad-tempered over

explanation.surface: A cricket over bowled in a foul mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Across can mean over, as in going across or over a bridge to the other side.

clue.text: Cliff Richard hit from good show

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the British singer's 1968 Eurovision song
second meaning: an exclamation of praise

explanation.surface: A Cliff Richard song comes from a successful show.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff Richard is a veteran British pop singer; this song came second at Eurovision in 1968.
explanation.definitionFit: The song title is also the word one says to praise success, like the old British exclamation 'good show'.

clue.text: Find leader of travelling people

indicators.note: the leader goes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Someone seeks the head of a group of travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace something is to track it down and locate it.

clue.text: Started unfolding it, organdie

indicators.note: unfolding fabric changes its shape, so these letters are laid out differently

explanation.surface: Someone began to unfold a piece of organdie, a fine sheer cotton.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or arise, so the past tense means started.

clue.text: Girl feeding pygmy rattlesnake

indicators.note: the answer is fed into the words that follow, lying inside them

explanation.surface: A girl is feeding a small venomous snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Myra is a female first name, so crosswords define it as girl.

clue.text: Silly threats involving little baby

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around, so one piece goes inside the other
silly suggests foolish disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Absurd threats are made against a small infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baby' looks like an infant but is a term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby and sweetheart are both affectionate terms of address for a loved one.

clue.text: First to ring city bank

indicators.note: first marks the opening letter as the one to keep

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: First ring the bank in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a financial institution but is the verb, as in bank on.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on something is to depend on it, so bank means rely here.
